dedupe_keys.name: u s underground coal mine methane emissions airborne observations and epa ghgrp comparison

description: This dataset quantifies methane emissions from US underground coal mines using airborne imaging spectrometer observations by Carbon Mapper, with the emissions that the mines report to the US EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (Subpart FF) for comparison. The Dataverse page says data are given for each ventilation shaft or gob well and aggregated to mine level by quarter from 2020 onwards, in three tables: individual plume observations linked to their vent and mine, mine-level quarterly emissions from both sources in kg per hour with one-sigma uncertainties, and an infrastructure table of shafts and wells. It accompanies the paper by Penn, Cusworth and co-authors on basin-scale inventories of coal mine methane, in review at Environmental Science and Technology in 2026. Version 1.0 was released on 21 March 2026 by Elise Penn as three downloadable tab-separated tables of about 86 KB in total, free under CC0 1.0, with national coverage of observed US mines. Caveats: only mines seen by Carbon Mapper are included, a flag marks where fewer than 75 percent of reported shafts were observed, and the paper was still in review. For simulation it gives located vent and mine emission rates for environmental impact and methane abatement scenarios of the coal mining sector, and shaft locations for mine asset layers. Related catalogue records include the China and the India and Australia coal mine methane inventories.
